descriptionAdvanced.en: The San Cristóbal Mine is a massive open-pit mining operation located in the Nor Lípez Province of the Potosí Department. It is one of the most significant industrial enterprises in Bolivia and ranks as one of the world's largest producers of zinc, lead, and silver. The project involved a monumental engineering feat, including the relocation of an entire 16th-century colonial village and its historic church to make way for the expanding pit. Operated by the Sumitomo Corporation, the mine utilizes state-of-the-art technology to process over 50,000 tons of rock daily in a remote, high-altitude desert environment. Historically, the area was known for its mineral wealth since colonial times, but modern large-scale industrialization began in the late 1990s, fundamentally transforming the regional economy.

en: The mine is located at an elevation of 3,756 meters above sea level.
San Cristóbal accounts for roughly half of Bolivia's total mineral exports by value.
The project includes one of the most advanced wastewater treatment and water recycling systems in the global mining industry.
The minerals are transported by a dedicated railway line to the port of Mejillones in Chile for global export.
